quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 40 Questions • Passing Score 35

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state safety standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no obvious defects.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop line before moving forward to see cross traffic better.
Ignore the stop line and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop line then proceed through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line before moving forward to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop line or stop sign. Then edge forward and stop again just short of where cross traffic enters your lane. Lean your body forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: What is often found in the center of the lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: An oily or greasy strip
questions.explanation: Oil drippings from cars form a strip in the center of each lane. It is usually safe for a motorcycle to ride on this strip unless the road is wet.

questions.question: The risk of head or neck injury is reduced:
questions.correctAnswerText: By wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Head and neck injuries are always a risk when riding a motorcycle, no matter your speed. Wearing a quality helmet properly greatly reduces the risk of these injuries.

questions.question: If a sign prohibits mopeds on a freeway:

options.text: Mopeds cannot be used on the freeway.
Mopeds can only be used on the freeway when traffic is moving smoothly.
Mopeds can be used on the freeway if they travel slower than 25 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mopeds cannot be used on the freeway.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to operate a motor-driven cycle or moped on a freeway or expressway when signs prohibit it.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume the passenger has traveled by motorcycle before.
Not assume the passenger has ridden a motorcycle before and explain what to do.
Not explain anything since they are only a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the passenger has ridden a motorcycle before and explain what to do.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle passenger needs to know how to ensure a safe ride for both themselves and the operator. Never assume the passenger already knows what to do. Give complete instructions before every ride.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:
questions.correctAnswerText: Cause control problems.
questions.explanation: Locking the brakes can cause control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and immediately re-apply it. If your rear brake locks on a surface with good grip, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection usually takes:

options.text: A few minutes and should be done once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
Over an hour and should be performed by a mechanic.
Over an hour and must only be done if you will be carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a thorough pre-ride inspection before every ride. It should usually take only a few minutes.

questions.question: When approaching an obstacle or uneven surface you cannot avoid, you should:

options.text: Make sure the motorcycle is leaning to one side.
Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle or uneven surface, approach it at close to a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as possible. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off your seat so your knees can absorb some force. Just before impact, roll on the throttle slightly to lighten the front end.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, motorcycle riders should be especially cautious of:

options.text: Motorists looking for a place to park.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars leaving their parking spaces.
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles, be cautious. Vehicles may pull away from the curb or leave parking spaces suddenly.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Slow down and let trains pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead. Always slow down when you approach a railroad crossing. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must wait for them to pass before you cross the tracks.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through the intersection carefully.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop completely and wait for a green arrow or light that allows you to turn in the direction you want.

questions.question: What should you do to lower the chance of a crash?

options.text: Use the correct position in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the correct position in your lane.
questions.explanation: To lower the chance of a crash, stay visible, use your signals, keep space between you and other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards, and be ready to react to changes.

questions.question: Should you wear gloves while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Yes. Your hands may get cold while riding.
Yes. They give you a better grip and protect your hands.
No. Gloves can get in the way of the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes. They give you a better grip and protect your hands.
questions.explanation: Wearing gloves while riding gives you a better grip and protects your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made of strong material.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for both the driver and passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for both the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have footrests for passengers. Having solid footing keeps your passenger from falling and pulling you off too.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Move to one side of your lane to let them share it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them get ahead of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up can make things more dangerous by encouraging them to tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: A good lane position should:

options.text: Help you see others and be seen.
Put you in other drivers' blind spots.
Make other drivers want to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What is one way to lower the risk of a crash?

options.text: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Do not look ahead while riding.
Ride in parts of your lane that are hard to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure others can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show what you plan to do. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and check your tires.
Pull over and check your chain.
Pull over and check your windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check your tires.
questions.explanation: A sudden change in handling may mean a tire has failed. If your motorcycle handles differently, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance to more than four seconds?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance on slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or in heavy traffic where other drivers may cut in front of you.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen frequently, so there is no need to worry about them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be fatal.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can be fatal.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow them to pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them get in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Riding faster may increase danger by making them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: To improve your chances of being seen, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or when visibility is poor.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on at all times.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: There is a 35 mph speed zone after the curve ahead.
Drive no slower than 35 mph around the upcoming curve.
Slow to 35 mph or less before the upcoming curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to 35 mph or less before the upcoming curve.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming road conditions. These signs often have speed plaques that show the safe speed for that area.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield does not replace a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Keep an adequate following distance behind other vehicles:

options.text: To give you time and space to spot and react to hazards.
To allow traffic counters to count you as a vehicle.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give you time and space to spot and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: An adequate following distance gives you enough space to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also gives you a better view of road hazards like potholes.

questions.question: While in a motor vehicle on a highway, it is:

options.text: Illegal to drink from or have open containers of alcohol.
Legal to drink alcohol if you're not driving.
Legal to drink alcohol if you're driving but not drunk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Illegal to drink from or have open containers of alcohol.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to operate a motor vehicle while under the influence of alcohol. No one—driver or passenger—may have an open container of alcohol in a moving vehicle.

questions.question: The best gear to wear when you ride is:

options.text: Any gear that helps protect you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any gear that helps protect you.
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. A DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing are best.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you on a motorcycle, watch out for:

options.text: Objects thrown from the other vehicle.
Wind gusts from the passing vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When being passed, watch for the vehicle's mirrors, wind gusts, and objects that passengers might throw. All of these can be dangerous to motorcyclists.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Road work is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn you about construction zones. This sign tells you that road work is ahead. Slow down and drive carefully through the work area.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of for best protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Leather or other durable materials provide the best protection for your hands when riding.

questions.question: In a crash, which of these does NOT help prevent serious injury?
questions.correctAnswerText: Have a windshield.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet, face protection, and protective clothing reduces injury risk. A windshield does not provide the same protection.

questions.question: Waiting one hour after one drink before riding:

options.text: Guarantees you cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Guarantees your riding skills will not be affected.
Is fine as long as you ride slowly.
May not fully remove alcohol from your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not fully remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: The body removes about one drink per hour on average, but this varies. The safest choice is not to ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is just part of riding a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause permanent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind noise can cause permanent hearing loss. Use ear protection while riding to prevent this damage.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Slow down and let trains pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This round sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop for trains.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. What should you wear to reduce crash risk?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to make yourself more visible to other drivers. This reduces your chance of being in a crash.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster your body removes it.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink faster than this, alcohol will build up in your system.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Does not work as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.
